platform: macOS 26.5 (25F71), arm64, Apple Silicon; debug build with the embedded frontend, isolated test mode (ADR 0003, macOS amendment), WKWebView driven through the test bridge (src-tauri/src/test_bridge.rs)
harness: node scripts/macos/m1-01-04-git-review.mjs --exe <exe> --port 9431 --base <tmp> --out-dir <dir> (scripts/macos/test-instance.mjs launch(), scripts/cdp-harness.mjs IPC trace)
method: One isolated instance drove the four tickets in one conversation, in a scratch repository with local identity (git config in the repo) and local bare remotes, all under the run's temp folder. The project folder was picked from the welcome screen (folder dialog answered through dialogQueue), the first message typed with Input.insertText and sent with a real Enter (Input.dispatchKeyEvent). Panel buttons were clicked in the page (element.click()), fields filled through React's value setter, as in the Windows record. Every repository claim was read back with /usr/bin/git, independently of the UI. The comment was written on the diff line of config.properties added during the run, sent with Send comment; the send_input call was read from the IPC trace and the turn's user entry and answer from the stored transcript. The queued comment's persistence was read after Page.reload.

limits: The comment asked for an explanation and a proposed fix in words, not an edit: the criterion is the anchored comment reaching the live engine and being answered. Any tool approval the engine requested during that turn was declined by the harness (approvalsDeclined), so nothing ran in the repository; a previous run without that guard showed the engine asking to run a read-only git diff on the comment.
The prompt names the file as 'config.properties (renamed from config.properties)' for an unrenamed file (oldPath always set): cosmetic, not macOS-specific, logged for the backlog.
